title: Shadow Deployment
shortDefinition: A strategy for safely validating a new AI model in production conditions by running it in parallel with the existing system without surfacing its outputs to users.
definition: Shadow deployment is a strategy for safely validating a new AI model in production conditions by running it in parallel alongside the existing system, processing real live traffic and generating predictions, without those predictions being shown to users or used for actual decisions — allowing the new model's behavior on real production data to be observed and compared against the current system before any real-world exposure. Shadow deployment eliminates the gap between how a model performs in staging tests and how it actually behaves on real production traffic, without users ever experiencing the new model's outputs until it's genuinely validated.

sections.title: How shadow deployment works
sections.description: The new model processes live traffic in parallel while the existing model continues to handle user-facing decisions.

content.text: The existing production model handles all actual user-facing decisions as normal. Simultaneously, the new candidate model processes the same live requests in parallel — its predictions are logged and compared against the current system's outputs, but never surfaced to users or used for any actual action. This lets you observe how the new model actually behaves on real-world traffic diversity (including rare, unexpected cases that staging tests didn't include) before any user is exposed to its decisions, catching unexpected behavior that might only appear in production data distributions.

items: Existing model — handles all actual user decisions.
New model — processes live requests in parallel.
Outputs logged — predictions are recorded but not used.
No user impact — users never see the new model's outputs.
Real traffic validation — catches issues only seen in production.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Shadow deployment eliminates the gap between staging performance and real production behavior — without any user exposure to unvalidated outputs.

sections.title: Shadow deployment vs. canary release: the key distinction

content.text: Shadow deployment and canary release both allow testing new models with exposure to real production traffic, but differ fundamentally in user impact. Shadow deployment: the new model runs silently — zero user impact, since its outputs are never actually used. Canary release: the new model's outputs are actually served to a small percentage of real users, making it a live partial deployment with genuine user exposure. Shadow deployment is appropriate when even limited real user exposure to an unvalidated model is unacceptable; canary release is appropriate once shadow testing has established sufficient confidence to justify limited real-world exposure.

content.title: Progressive validation
content.text: Shadow deployment tests without any user impact. Canary release exposes a small subset to live outputs. Both are valuable in a progressive deployment strategy.

"Can shadow deployment replace staging environment testing?" — No — shadow deployment complements staging testing by providing real production traffic validation that staging can't fully replicate, not replacing the initial staging validation that catches basic issues before any production exposure.

"Do we need shadow deployment, or can we go straight to a canary release?" — ClickMasters recommends shadow deployment before canary release for any model making consequential decisions — it's the safest way to observe real production behavior before any user is actually exposed to a new model's outputs.

"Does shadow deployment significantly increase infrastructure cost?" — It requires running the new model in parallel with the existing system temporarily, adding some compute cost during the shadow period; ClickMasters scopes this cost as part of deployment planning.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of shadow deployment

content.text: Shadow deployment has limitations. It adds infrastructure cost and complexity for running parallel models. Shadow testing requires sufficient traffic volume and duration to be meaningful. Output comparison metrics must be carefully defined to avoid misleading conclusions. Shadow deployment doesn't guarantee the new model will perform well in live use since user behavior may differ when outputs are not surfaced. The approach also requires additional monitoring and logging infrastructure.

items: Infrastructure cost — parallel models add compute expense.
Traffic requirements — needs sufficient volume for validation.
Metric design — comparison metrics must be carefully defined.
User behavior gap — live performance may differ.
Monitoring overhead — requires additional logging and monitoring.
Temporary nature — shadow deployment is a time-limited phase.

content.title: Important
content.text: Shadow deployment is a validation phase, not a permanent state. Plan for clear duration criteria and a defined path to full deployment or rollback.

Implementing shadow deployment effectively requires careful infrastructure design, metric definition, and decision criteria. The following practices can help ensure your shadow deployment provides meaningful validation.

content.title: Recommended approach:

Ensure sufficient traffic volume for meaningful validation.
Run shadow deployment for a sufficient duration to capture traffic variety.

content.title: Key metric
content.text: Measure the difference between new and current model outputs — if the new model consistently deviates in ways that would affect decisions, investigate before proceeding.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about shadow deployment

items.question: What types of AI model updates benefit most from shadow deployment?
items.answer: Models making consequential decisions (fraud detection, healthcare risk scoring, credit decisions) where even limited unvalidated real-user exposure carries meaningful risk benefit most from shadow deployment before any live release.

items.question: Does shadow deployment significantly increase infrastructure cost?
items.answer: It requires running the new model in parallel with the existing system temporarily, adding some compute cost during the shadow period; ClickMasters scopes this cost as part of deployment planning.

items.question: How long should a shadow deployment run before making a go/no-go decision?
items.answer: Long enough to observe sufficient traffic volume and variety to be confident the new model behaves consistently across real production data diversity; ClickMasters recommends a minimum traffic volume based on your specific decision context rather than an arbitrary time period.

items.question: Can shadow deployment catch issues that staging tests would miss?
items.answer: Yes — this is its primary value: real production traffic includes rare and unexpected input patterns that even well-designed staging tests don't fully capture, which shadow deployment can surface safely before user exposure.

items.question: How long does shadow deployment infrastructure take to build?
items.answer: 8–22 weeks depending on the number of models and comparison reporting requirements.

items.question: When do we move from shadow deployment to a canary release?
items.answer: Once shadow comparison confirms the new model's outputs are consistently acceptable across sufficient real traffic diversity — ClickMasters defines specific comparison criteria for this decision before shadow deployment begins.

items.question: What is the difference between shadow deployment and A/B testing?
items.answer: A/B testing serves different model outputs to different user groups to measure business impact. Shadow deployment runs the new model in parallel without serving its outputs to anyone — it's about validating technical behavior before any user exposure.

items.question: Can shadow deployment be used for LLM-based applications?
items.answer: Yes — shadow deployment is valuable for LLM applications where a new prompt design, model version, or RAG configuration needs validation on real traffic before user exposure.

items.question: What is the relationship between shadow deployment and model drift monitoring?
items.answer: Shadow deployment validates a new model version before deployment. Model drift monitoring tracks performance of a deployed model over time. Both are complementary — shadow for changes, drift for ongoing health.

items.question: What is the difference between shadow deployment and offline evaluation?
items.answer: Offline evaluation uses historical data. Shadow deployment uses real-time production traffic. Shadow provides more realistic validation because it uses current live traffic patterns and user behavior.
